name: What is the difference between working with a hands-on contractor versus a large remodeling firm?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between working with a hands-on contractor versus a large remodeling firm?

acceptedAnswer.text: A working owner-operator acts as both the primary project coordinator and an active craftsman on the jobsite, whereas corporate project managers primarily supervise from off-site. With a hands-on contractor, the person who writes your estimate is actively managing the framing, drywall, or finish carpentry, ensuring details discussed during planning are executed correctly. Corporate management companies often rotate site managers or rely completely on external crews, which can occasionally lead to communication gaps. The trade-off is that smaller, hands-on operations take on fewer projects simultaneously, requiring homeowners to plan schedules around limited calendar availability.
acceptedAnswer.description: A hands-on contractor directly oversees and performs key work on-site for clearer communication, while larger firms use off-site managers and rotating trade crews.
